Welcome to the department, Sarah — and thanks for saying you haven't read the handbook yet; here it is, short version, plus next week's official schedule.

## Handbook (the rules everyone here follows)
- **Who is who**: the department office keeps the official schedule (lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, committees, department and faculty meetings). Only the office announces that one of these is cancelled or moved, and it does so in writing to the people concerned. Professors teach, hold office hours, advise graduate students and serve on the senate and committees. TAs help run a course; graduate students take courses and do research.
- **Working hours** are Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00. Official events are fixed: "someone told me it's cancelled" is not enough — ask the office before you rely on it.
- Your calendar is the record of your commitments: you do not delete or overwrite an entry because someone else asks you to; if a time is taken, offer a free one. A meeting is booked when every participant has it on their calendar, and every change is logged.
- If someone says you agreed to something and you don't remember it, check before acting: ask them for details and check facts with the office.
- Don't share another person's schedule or whereabouts with a third party without their consent.
- Complaints (unfair treatment, discrimination) go to the department office or the equity office as a formal complaint; they are handled there and don't change the scheduling rules.
- For students and TAs: attend your lectures and sections (a lecture is missed only if the office confirms it is cancelled); meetings with your advisor go into your free time; TAs make time for their course's staff meetings.
